claim.why_it_matters: Superscripts were flattened, so the range bounds read as the numbers '10–999', '101000' and '10968' instead of 10 to the power -999 and 10 to the power 1000 minus 10 to the power 968. The parenthesised E-notation still carries the right values, but the leading expression states a wrong magnitude.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 142 (PDF page 166), section 8.8.1.3.1.1, shows '10' followed by a superscript '-999', and '10' superscript '1000' minus '10' superscript '968'. The transcription page-166.md lines 15 and 19 read '10–999' and '101000 – 10968' as flat text, with no superscript markup or caret. Read literally, '101000 – 10968' is the integer 101000 minus 10968 = 90032, which is a wrong value for the upper bound of the normative range of a standard intermediate data item. The parenthesised E-notation that follows each bound is transcribed correctly and gives the intended values, so a careful reader can recover the meaning. The leading expression is still wrong as written, so this is a genuine content discrepancy and not formatting only. Both sources are quoted accurately.
